event_date_basis: Broadcom's own press-release page carries JSON-LD "datePublished": "2026-06-24T09:00:48-0400" and the dateline "SAN FRANCISCO and PALO ALTO, Calif., June  24, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE)". OpenAI's official news RSS lists the same item with pubDate "Wed, 24 Jun 2026 06:00:00 GMT". Announcement date and publication date are therefore the same day, 2026-06-24, on both sides. The EFFECTIVE date is different and must not be conflated: the Broadcom release says the platform is "designed for initial deployment by the end of 2026", and Hock Tan's quote says gigawatt-scale data centres "with Microsoft and other partners beginning in 2026". There is no stated ship date, general-availability date or purchase date of any kind.

sources.title: OpenAI and Broadcom Unveil LLM-Optimized Intelligence Processor
OpenAI and Broadcom announce strategic collaboration to deploy 10 gigawatts of OpenAI-designed AI accelerators

verified_facts.fact: The announcement was made jointly by OpenAI and Broadcom on 2026-06-24. Broadcom's press-release page carries the dateline and the machine-readable publication date 2026-06-24T09:00:48-04:00.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: SAN FRANCISCO and PALO ALTO, Calif., June  24, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- OpenAI and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) today unveiled Jalapeño

verified_facts.fact: The product name is spelled Jalapeño, with the tilde n, in Broadcom's release and in OpenAI's own feed description. It is NOT spelled 'Jalapeno' in the official text.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Jalapeño

verified_facts.fact: Broadcom's own headline for the announcement is 'OpenAI and Broadcom Unveil LLM-Optimized Intelligence Processor'. OpenAI's own feed title for the same day is different: 'OpenAI and Broadcom unveil LLM-optimized inference chip'. Both are official; they are two companies' headlines for one announcement.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI and Broadcom Unveil LLM-Optimized Intelligence Processor

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI's official news feed lists the item on Wed, 24 Jun 2026 06:00:00 GMT, category 'Company', link https://openai.com/index/openai-broadcom-jalapeno-inference-chip, with the one-line description: 'OpenAI and Broadcom introduce Jalapeño, a custom AI chip built for LLM inference to improve performance, efficiency, and scale across AI systems.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI and Broadcom introduce Jalapeño, a custom AI chip built for LLM inference to improve performance, efficiency, and scale across AI systems.

verified_facts.fact: Broadcom calls Jalapeño 'OpenAI's first Intelligence Processor' and 'the first AI accelerator in a multi-generation compute platform the companies are building together'. 'Intelligence Processor' is the official category word; the release never calls it a GPU.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) today unveiled Jalapeño, OpenAI’s first Intelligence Processor: an accelerator architected around OpenAI’s vision for the future of LLM inference, and the first AI accelerator in a multi-generation compute platform the companies are building together to make advanced AI faster, more reliable, and more accessible to more people.

verified_facts.fact: The release opens with five bullets: 'Built from the ground up for current and future LLMs across the industry'; 'Developed from design to production in nine months, accelerated by OpenAI's models'; 'Will deliver performance per watt better than current state-of-the-art, based on early testing'; 'Expands OpenAI's full-stack platform, from products to models and now to chips'; 'To be deployed at gigawatt scale with data center partners, over multiple generations'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Built from the ground up for current and future LLMs across the industry / Developed from design to production in nine months, accelerated by OpenAI’s models / Will deliver performance per watt better than current state-of-the-art, based on early testing / Expands OpenAI’s full-stack platform, from products to models and now to chips / To be deployed at gigawatt scale with data center partners, over multiple generations

verified_facts.fact: Division of labour as officially stated: OpenAI designed the chip from scratch, informed by its roadmap of models, kernels, serving systems and product needs; Broadcom and Celestica help industrialize the platform through chip implementation, board and rack system integration, high-performance networking and scalable production systems.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI designed the chip from scratch around its deep understanding of LLM fundamentals, informed by its roadmap of models, kernels, serving systems, and product needs, with partners Broadcom and Celestica, helping industrialize the platform through chip implementation, board, rack system integration, high-performance networking, and scalable production systems.

verified_facts.fact: A third company, Celestica, is named as a partner for board, rack and system expertise. Only three companies are named on the build side: OpenAI, Broadcom, Celestica.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: combining OpenAI-designed accelerators with Broadcom silicon implementation, networking, and connectivity technologies; and Celestica’s board, rack and system expertise

verified_facts.fact: The one Broadcom component named by product family is Tomahawk networking silicon.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Broadcom’s silicon implementation and networking technologies, including Tomahawk networking silicon, help bring the platform to large-scale production.

verified_facts.fact: A physical handover is described: the chip was delivered to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and President Greg Brockman by Broadcom President and CEO Hock Tan and Semiconductor Solutions President Charlie Kawwas.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Jalapeño was delivered to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and President Greg Brockman by Broadcom President and CEO Hock Tan and Semiconductor Solutions President Charlie Kawwas, marking an important step in OpenAI’s strategy to build the full stack behind its models and products.

verified_facts.fact: As of the announcement the chip exists as engineering samples, not shipping product: samples are running ML workloads in the lab at production target frequency and power, including the model GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Engineering samples of the Jalapeño chip are running ML workloads in the lab at production target frequency and power, including GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI says it is still measuring final performance; the only performance statement offered is directional, with no number: performance per watt 'substantially better than current state-of-the-art', based on early testing.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: While OpenAI is still measuring final performance, early testing shows that Jalapeño will deliver performance per watt substantially better than current state-of-the-art.

verified_facts.fact: Broadcom says a detailed technical report on performance 'will be presented in the coming months' - i.e. the measured numbers were deliberately not published on 2026-06-24.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: A detailed technical report on performance will be presented in the coming months.

verified_facts.fact: Architecture claim, stated qualitatively only: the design reduces data movement and balances compute, memory and networking so that realized utilization is 'much closer to theoretical peak performance'. No utilization percentage is given.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The architecture reduces data movement and balances compute, memory, and networking resources to achieve realized utilization much closer to theoretical peak performance.

verified_facts.fact: Design-philosophy claim: Jalapeño is 'a blank-slate design for modern LLM inference, not a general-purpose accelerator adapted from earlier AI workloads', informed by the systems OpenAI runs across ChatGPT, Codex, the API and future agentic products, while also being designed for current and future LLMs across the industry.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Jalapeño is a blank-slate design for modern LLM inference, not a general-purpose accelerator adapted from earlier AI workloads. It is informed by the systems OpenAI runs every day across ChatGPT, Codex, the API, and future agentic products, while also being designed for current and future LLMs across the industry.

verified_facts.fact: Stated design goal (a goal, not a measured result): combine the power and throughput of today's leading AI accelerators with latency closer to the fastest specialized inference systems, making it suited to interactive LLM products at scale.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The goal is to combine the power and throughput of today’s leading AI accelerators with latency closer to the fastest specialized inference systems, making Jalapeño well suited for interactive LLM products at scale.

verified_facts.fact: Nine months is the headline schedule figure, but the two places it appears say different things. The bullet says 'Developed from design to production in nine months'; the body says 'co-developed from initial design to manufacturing tape-out in just nine months'. Tape-out is not production. Use the body wording.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Jalapeño was co-developed from initial design to manufacturing tape-out in just nine months

verified_facts.fact: Broadcom hedges the speed record explicitly: the programme 'represents what may be the fastest ASIC development cycle ever achieved in high-performance advanced semiconductors'. 'may be' is in the official text; it is not asserted as established.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: the custom AI accelerator program represents what may be the fastest ASIC development cycle ever achieved in high-performance advanced semiconductors

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI's own models were used to accelerate parts of the chip's design and optimization process, and the release draws the loop explicitly: the same models served to users are helping improve the infrastructure used to run future models.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: That speed reflects deep software-hardware co-development with OpenAI’s engineering teams, Broadcom’s silicon implementation expertise, and the use of OpenAI models to accelerate parts of the design and optimization process.

verified_facts.fact: Deployment timing as officially stated: the multi-generation compute platform is 'designed for initial deployment by the end of 2026, and expanding in the years ahead'. 'Designed for' is the official hedge - it is not a committed launch date.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Jalapeño is the first step in a multi-generation compute platform designed for initial deployment by the end of 2026, and expanding in the years ahead

verified_facts.fact: Deployment scale as officially stated: 'To be deployed at gigawatt scale with data center partners, over multiple generations'. No number of gigawatts, chips, racks or sites is attached to Jalapeño anywhere in this release.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: To be deployed at gigawatt scale with data center partners, over multiple generations

verified_facts.fact: Hock Tan (President and CEO, Broadcom) names one data-centre partner: 'By co-developing our industry-leading silicon directly with OpenAI, we are enabling the deployment of gigawatt scale data centers with Microsoft and other partners beginning in 2026.' Microsoft is the only partner named in the whole release besides Celestica.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Our collaboration with OpenAI represents a fundamental commitment to scaling the physical infrastructure required for the next decade of AI. This is just the beginning of a multi-generation roadmap. By co-developing our industry-leading silicon directly with OpenAI, we are enabling the deployment of gigawatt scale data centers with Microsoft and other partners beginning in 2026.

verified_facts.fact: Richard Ho is identified as the person 'who leads OpenAI's hardware program'. His quote: the architecture was optimized around 'the kernels, memory movement, networking, and serving patterns that matter most for frontier AI models', and 'Based on early testing, Jalapeño will efficiently execute our most important workloads close to the hardware's theoretical limits.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Jalapeño was designed from the ground up for LLM inference using detailed insights from our close collaboration with OpenAI researchers. We optimized the architecture around the kernels, memory movement, networking, and serving patterns that matter most for frontier AI models. Based on early testing, Jalapeño will efficiently execute our most important workloads close to the hardware’s theoretical limits.

verified_facts.fact: Greg Brockman is titled 'President and Co-Founder, OpenAI' in this release. His quote frames the chip as part of a full-stack strategy to make compute more abundant so AI is 'faster, more reliable, more affordable for people and businesses'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The world is moving to a compute-powered economy. Jalapeño is part of our long-term full-stack infrastructure strategy to make compute more abundant, resulting in AI which is faster, more reliable, more affordable for people and businesses, and can be used to solve more important problems. By designing more of the stack ourselves, we can serve more intelligence with greater efficiency and keep pushing advanced AI toward broader access.

verified_facts.fact: The release carries an explicit forward-looking-statements notice under Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, naming the Jalapeño delivery and the gigawatt-scale data-centre deployment as forward-looking, and saying 'undue reliance should not be placed on such statements'. This is the company's own instruction not to treat the deployment language as fact.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: These statements include, but are not limited to, statements regarding Broadcom’s collaboration with OpenAI in delivering Jalapeño to OpenAI and Broadcom helping bring OpenAI’s full-stack platform to large-scale production to enable the deployment of gigawatt scale datacenters. ... Accordingly, undue reliance should not be placed on such statements.

verified_facts.fact: BACKGROUND (2025-10-13, a separate earlier announcement): OpenAI and Broadcom announced 'a collaboration for 10 gigawatts of custom AI accelerators', with OpenAI designing the accelerators and systems and Broadcom developing and deploying them.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI and Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO) today announced a collaboration for 10 gigawatts of custom AI accelerators. OpenAI will design the accelerators and systems, which will be developed and deployed in partnership with Broadcom.

verified_facts.fact: BACKGROUND (2025-10-13): the stated rollout window is 'Broadcom to deploy racks of AI accelerator and network systems targeted to start in the second half of 2026, to complete by end of 2029'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Broadcom to deploy racks of AI accelerator and network systems targeted to start in the second half of 2026, to complete by end of 2029

verified_facts.fact: BACKGROUND (2025-10-13): the racks are 'scaled entirely with Ethernet and other connectivity solutions from Broadcom', with deployments 'across OpenAI's facilities and partner data centers'. Charlie Kawwas's quote lists Broadcom's Ethernet, PCIe and optical connectivity portfolio.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: The racks, scaled entirely with Ethernet and other connectivity solutions from Broadcom, will meet surging global demand for AI, with deployments across OpenAI’s facilities and partner data centers.

verified_facts.fact: BACKGROUND (2025-10-13): the commercial status then was a term sheet, not a completed contract - 'The two companies have signed a term sheet to deploy racks incorporating the AI accelerators and Broadcom networking solutions', alongside 'long-standing agreements on the co-development and supply of the AI accelerators'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI and Broadcom have long-standing agreements on the co-development and supply of the AI accelerators. The two companies have signed a term sheet to deploy racks incorporating the AI accelerators and Broadcom networking solutions.

verified_facts.fact: BACKGROUND (2025-10-13): the release states 'OpenAI has grown to over 800 million weekly active users'. This figure is as of 2025-10-13 and must be dated if used; no user figure appears in the 2026-06-24 release.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI has grown to over 800 million weekly active users and strong adoption across global enterprises, small businesses, and developers.

verified_facts.fact: BACKGROUND (2025-10-13): OpenAI's own feed summarises that announcement as 'a multi-year partnership to deploy 10 gigawatts of OpenAI-designed AI accelerators, co-developing next-generation systems and Ethernet solutions to power scalable, energy-efficient AI infrastructure by 2029.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI and Broadcom announce a multi-year partnership to deploy 10 gigawatts of OpenAI-designed AI accelerators, co-developing next-generation systems and Ethernet solutions to power scalable, energy-efficient AI infrastructure by 2029.

verified_facts.fact: FOLLOW-UP (2026-08-25, after the event date of this article): OpenAI's official feed carries 'Jalapeño’s first results show industry-leading speed and efficiency in AI inference' (category Engineering, 07:00 GMT), described as 'Jalapeño is a custom inference chip from OpenAI that delivers faster, more power-efficient AI inference, with higher throughput and lower latency for modern models.' The article page itself is 403 in this container, so NOTHING beyond this one line may be written about it.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Jalapeño’s first results show industry-leading speed and efficiency in AI inference

verified_facts.fact: FOLLOW-UP CONTEXT (2026-08-25, 07:05 GMT): OpenAI's feed also carries 'The full stack behind abundant intelligence', described as 'OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar explains how advances across chips, compute, models, and products compound to deliver more useful intelligence at greater scale and lower cost.' Same caveat: page unreadable, one line only.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar explains how advances across chips, compute, models, and products compound to deliver more useful intelligence at greater scale and lower cost.

not_said: NO PRICE of any kind. The chip is not sold; there is no unit price, no per-token price, no cost-per-inference figure, and no statement that any ChatGPT or API price will change.

NO MANUFACTURING DETAIL. The release never names a foundry (TSMC is not mentioned), never gives a process node, never gives die size, transistor count, package type, clock frequency or power draw in watts. 'Production target frequency and power' is used without any number.
NO MEMORY SPECIFICATION. HBM, memory capacity and memory bandwidth are not mentioned at all. 'memory movement' and 'memory' appear only as architectural words.

NO BENCHMARK NUMBER. Not one measured figure is published: no tokens/second, no latency in ms, no perf-per-watt ratio, no percentage, no comparison table. The release says OpenAI 'is still measuring final performance' and promises a technical report 'in the coming months'.
NO NAMED COMPETITOR AND NO COMPARISON BASELINE. 'current state-of-the-art' is never defined; NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU and Trainium are not mentioned anywhere.

NO STATED LINK TO THE 10 GIGAWATT FIGURE. The 2026-06-24 release says 'gigawatt scale' but gives no number, and never says Jalapeño is the accelerator covered by the 2025-10-13 10 GW collaboration. Treating them as the same programme is the reader's inference, not an official statement.
NO QUANTITY. Number of chips, racks, systems or data-centre sites is not stated.
NO EXACT DEPLOYMENT DATE. Only 'designed for initial deployment by the end of 2026' and 'beginning in 2026'. No month, no region, no site list.

NO EXTERNAL SALE. The release says the design is flexible enough to work with 'all LLMs' and with 'current and future LLMs across the industry', but it NEVER says the chip will be sold, rented or made available to any company other than OpenAI, and it names no third-party customer.
NO CONSUMER-FACING EFFECT. Nothing says ChatGPT, Codex or the API will become faster or cheaper on any date, or that any user-visible change will happen at all.
NO REGIONAL INFORMATION. Taiwan, Asia and any country other than the US (San Francisco / Palo Alto datelines) are absent. No statement about which regions the deployed capacity serves.
NO MODEL-SUPPORT LIST. GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark is named only as a workload running on engineering samples in the lab. There is no statement about which production models will run on it.
NO ROLE DETAIL FOR CELESTICA beyond 'board, rack and system expertise', and no contract, value or term for Celestica or Broadcom.
NO FINANCIAL TERMS of the OpenAI-Broadcom arrangement in the 2026-06-24 release: no order value, no volume commitment, no duration. The 2025-10-13 release only goes as far as 'a term sheet'.
NO REGULATORY, EXPORT-CONTROL OR SUPPLY-CHAIN CONDITION is mentioned in either release.
NO SECOND-GENERATION DETAIL. 'multi-generation roadmap' and 'over multiple generations' are asserted with no names, dates or specifications for any later generation.
